description.narrative:
Sverige kommer att stödja NEC, en civil organisation från Moldavien, för genomförandet av kärnstödsaktiviteter försedda av NEC Strategiska plan och RAF under 2020 – 2023. Kärnstöd beviljas för att stärka den institutionella kapaciteten och för att stödja genomförandet av NEC medellång sikt Strategisk plan 2020—2023. Huvudmålet och det förväntade resultatet av kärnverksamheten är att NEC bidrar till att utveckla journalisternas kapacitet att återspegla miljöfrågor.
Under den förberedande processen för insatsen, så har Sida’s principer och centrala prioriteringar för samarbetet med civilsamhällesorganisationer diskuterats med partnern. NEC ställer sig bakom Sidas gemensamma utgångspunkter för samarbete. Ambassaden tillsammans med NEC kommer att ha en kontinuerlig, öppen och transparent dialog om etiska och andra värdebaserade frågor.

Sweden will support NEC, a civil society organisation from Moldova, to implement core support activities provided by NEC Strategic Plan and RAF during 2020 - 2023.
Core support is granted to strengthen institutional capacities and to assist the implementation of NEC medium term Strategic Plan 2020-2023. The main objective and expected result of core activities is that NEC contributes to developing the capacities of journalists in reflecting environmental issues.
Principal values for Sida and cooperation partners were shared and discussed as guidance during initial consultations on the contribution/project between programme coordinator and organization. NEC is open to endorse Sida's common starting points for cooperation. The Embassy, together with NEC will have a continuous, open and transparent dialogue on ethical and other value based issues.

description.narrative:
Among theresults of the implementation of the NEC Strategy are: Increased capacities and vigilance of the decision makers (local public authorities, decentralized authorities in environment and health) in water resources management; Increased public vigilance and involvement in water resources protection, as well as change of behaviour of water users; Increased capacities of LPA in integrated water resources management; Enhanced capacities of the authorities in the implementation of the integrated waste management system; Increased volume of separately collected waste; Sustainable agricultural model - School Garden established in the rural areas; ________________________________________________ The content of the Progress report reflects the agreed structure of NEC Results Assessment Framework (RAF) - the strategic document that determines the work of the association in the period 2020-2024. According to RAF all the activities of the Association are performed in one of the four strategic areas (1, 2, 3, 4), as follows: Waste and Water Management; Green Economy and Climate Change; Organisational Development and Increased Visibility.
Throughout 2023, the Organisation has achieved remarkable success across all four strategic priorities mentioned above, as follows:
A large-scale national campaign on World Cleanup Day saw 6,000 volunteers from over 120 localities participating, resulting in the collection of more than 500 cubic meters of waste from green areas. Contribution to the National Program for the Extension and Rehabilitation of Forests by organizing the annual planting campaign. This included planting 78 hectares of land in Geamna, Anenii Noi, and establishing river protection strips along the Dniester in Molovata village, Dubsari district, with over 50 participants including village residents, students, and APL representatives, covering approximately 2 km of the shore. Twelve schools from both banks of the Dniester developed and executed environmental projects and actions. The Small Grants Program "Environment, Adaptation to Climate Change, and Ecosystems" continued into its second edition, selecting five beneficiary NGOs from across the country. These NGOs implemented projects addressing waste management in localities, rehabilitating river protection, and educating and training village inhabitants. Six springs that directly feed surface water sources (rivers and streams) were rehabilitated in various localities: Nistru in Cremenciug, Rut in Furceni and Jevreni, Tigheci in Pleeni, Racova in Tîrnova, and Larga in Larga Noua. Four localities improved their waste management systems: Vadul-Racov, oldneti, Soroca, Molovata, and Oxentea, Dubsari. The EcoAlert tool was promoted, with 348 notifications registered (253 at the end of 2022 and 188 in 2021), of which 321 were resolved (158 in 2021), and only 14 were rejected. Support for School Gardens continued, with four new schools joining the network at the end of 2022. These schools implemented the School Garden project in 2023 and participated in local and national fairs with their garden products. Four educational institutions advanced enough to offer support to other schools, teachers, and students through consultations, studio tours, and training. The NEC Facebook page gained 886 new followers, totaling 6,494 likes, with an annual organic reach of nearly 265,000. There were 177 posts on the Facebook page, 138 mentions and tags on other accounts/pages, and over 50 media appearances in newspapers, online portals, TV, and radio shows. Visibility and awareness-raising efforts led to CNM being recognized and followed by citizens, with five videos produced: two descriptive videos of WCD 2023, one video on the Pesticide Site restoration, and summaries of WCD 2023. During World Cleanup Day 2023 (September 15 and 16), more than 1,000 volunteers from about 120 localities collected approximately 4,000 cubic meters of waste, primarily from rivers, springs, and lakes. One study analyzed the impact of dams in the Dniester River basin, and one communication strategy was developed for the National Program for Forest Extension and Rehabilitation.
To conclude, the achievements of 2023 can be highlighted as follows: the Organisation has effectively engaged a broad spectrum of the population through its diverse project activities. From large-scale campaigns like World Cleanup Day to targeted initiatives such as the Small Grants Program and School Gardens, their efforts have clearly made a significant impact across various communities. _______________________________________________ The 2024 Progress Report outlines the yearly organizations achievements and also results from January to April 2024, supported in part by funding from Sweden. This four-month period falls within the no-cost extension of the Core Support, approved by Sida in October 2023. The extension was requested to utilize remaining funds and to expand the scope of environmental activities.
This report is structured in accordance with NECs Results Assessment Framework for 20202023, which focuses on four key strategic areas: Water, Waste, Green Economy & Climate Change, and Organizational Development. Each chapter highlights the achieved outcomes, delivered outputs, and relevant cross-cutting initiatives.
In 2024, NEC delivered impactful results across its strategic focus areas, engaging communities, schools, and authorities in advancing shared environmental objectives:
- Eco-coala WASH Initiative: Partnered with 20 schools, reaching over 7,700 students and community members. - Youth Empowerment: Organized two regional summer camps, training 64 young leaders in WASH and climate action. - Capacity Building: Provided project management, environmental leadership, and WASH training to more than 200 teachers and students. - Afforestation Efforts: Established 14 Baby Forests in schools through the USFS-supported program, planting 4 hectares of diverse species under the #forestgeneration initiative. - Riparian Restoration: Planted 3 hectares of riparian belt along the Nistru River near Molovata. - Site Remediation: Cleaned and replanted a contaminated site in Molovata with native vegetation. - Forestry Education: Conducted two workshops for 36 young foresters and ecology students. - Water Governance: Developed and promoted a national Financing Roadmap for Dniester Basin water management (Cycle II), engaging over 70 stakeholders. - Sub-basin Support: Strengthened six Sub-basin Committees. - Forest Rehabilitation: Contributed to the National Program for Forest Extension and Rehabilitation, supporting maintenance of 56 hectares of planted land in Anenii Noi district. - EcoAlert Impact: Resolved 51 environmental cases through the EcoAlert app. - School Garden Network: Sustained a functional network of 12 schools cultivating eco-entrepreneurial projects. - Public Engagement: Expanded outreach with 6,500 likes, 7,200 Facebook followers, 73,000 organic reach, and 28 media features. - Resource Mobilization: Secured over $134,000 in additional project funding beyond Core Sida support. These accomplishments reflect NECs growing influence and operational capacity as a leading national actor in environmental protection and education.
The lessons learnt and conslussions of the 2024 year:
- Youth-Led Impact: Environmental initiatives driven by young people continue to yield meaningful, high-impact results. - Strategic Partnerships: Collaborations with academic institutions (e.g., ICAS, College of Ecology) and Local Public Authorities (LPAs) significantly amplify project effectiveness and outreach. - Digital Engagement: Tools like EcoAlert play a pivotal role in fostering civic involvement and environmental accountability. - Afforestation Lessons: Successful planting efforts hinge on optimal timing, thorough soil preparation, and consistent post-planting care. - Integrated Approaches: Cross-sector collaboration is essential for advancing sustainable water and waste management solutions.
